claims.exact_passage: For held-out online news from late 2019, the natural choice is the **WMT19 news translation test set** (`newstest2019`), the en–de test set used in the Fourth Conference on Machine Translation. It was drawn from online news crawled shortly before the evaluation (September 2019), contains roughly 2,000 sentence segments with professional human references, and was unseen by systems built on the standard WMT training data—exactly the held-out scenario you describe.
claims.rationale: WMT19 uses September–November 2018 sources and was already released April 8, 2019; September 2019 source acquisition is incompatible with that release. Roughly 2000 segments agrees with official 1997, so that component is supported.
claims.materiality: primary date-fit endorsement C1; count supported

claims.exact_passage: was unseen by systems built on the standard WMT training data
claims.rationale: A narrower historical constrained-training reading is reasonable and consistent with unseen task intent; not evidence about the present two systems. The source supplies no universal corpus-overlap verification.
claims.materiality: historical scope; do not infer present contamination

entries.C4_boundary_note: The historically qualified standard-WMT-training assertion is narrower than A02’s major-baseline ensure/prevent language. Keep any C4 concern distinct from the directly established C1 mismatch. Do not treat an omitted modern-contamination caveat alone as failure.

claims.exact_passage: Use the WMT20 English–German General MT test set, often distributed as newstest2020 or wmt20-en-de. It is a public, held-out test set built from recent news material and is the standard choice for comparing English-to-German MT systems on late-2019 online news.
claims.rationale: Referent newstest2020 / WMT20 is identifiable despite General MT nomenclature. Official news task source period and direction match.

claims.exact_passage: Because the set is held out from the public WMT training data, it reduces the risk that models have memorized the evaluation sentences.
claims.rationale: Historically separated shared-task testing supports the narrower intent. Exact absence from every released training corpus is not independently audited here. Risk reduction is qualified and does not promise absence in present model training.
claims.materiality: qualified historical/risk statement, not verified absence guarantee
